title: Durable activation authority ledger
description: Objective: provide the missing durable all-or-none persistence contract for one execution activation without adding ad-hoc SQLite schema. Depends on task-c956fd56f0d24e84a33644934982828f and task-311adb23a3964146a25fa8bddf7123e9. Deliverable: a focused daemon activation-ledger codec/reader/commit adapter that stores one canonical EffectActivationCommitted event containing the claim successor closure plus the runner activation commit and activated budget/slot successors. Derive a dedicated aggregate id from `(effect aggregateId,idempotencyKey)`, always commit it from expected version 0, and use the existing aggregate-head primary key plus globally unique domain-event id set to the grantId to enforce semantic uniqueness. Consumer: task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d. NOT in scope: recovery embargo decisions, HTTP registry wiring, provider launch, schema/table migrations, or constructing claim/activation outcomes. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: The exact versioned activation record/codec preserves and digest-binds active lease, dimension/attempt-bound ACTIVE provider slot, post-reservation budget view plus ACTIVATED reservation, ACTIVE effect intent, RUNNING attempt, UNUSED grant, predecessor intent/attempt versions, and activation digest.

The commit adapter derives the target aggregate id injectively from `(aggregateId,idempotencyKey)`, requires expected aggregate version 0, uses the grantId as the unique business event id, and appends the decision/event/authority record in one existing @moe/store transaction.

Same-command replay returns the original durable record without rerunning apply; a distinct command for the same aggregate/idempotency pair or the same grantId accepts exactly once and otherwise pins the exact EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT or store uniqueness refusal with zero duplicate events.

The production reader requires exactly one correctly typed event whose payload, derived aggregate id, event id/grant id, versions and digest agree; absent, truncated, extra or malformed evidence returns a typed UNKNOWN/refusal and never reconstructs authority.

Focused concurrency and injected-throw tests assert exact decision disposition/code/layer plus event counts, prove no partial attempt/slot/lease/effect/grant/budget record is observable, and assert every generated race set has positive cardinality.

The focused daemon/store gates pass, a mutation of the production aggregate-id or expected-version guard reddens the named replay/race test, and task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d is recorded as the production consumer.
taskRails: Use existing @moe/store aggregate-head, event-id, command-decision and commit-with-apply authorities; do not create SQLite objects or execute daemon-owned ad-hoc DDL.
TDD every behavior; refusal tests pin exact stable code and refusing layer, and zero-authority assertions include a positive accepted control through the production adapter.
Never persist a partial activation tuple or optimistically reconstruct missing bytes; unreadable evidence is UNKNOWN.
Use only public package roots across boundaries; target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY IS DISJOINT AND NON-FLATTENING. implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-codec.ts plus its `.js` bridge: encode, decode, digest, and the reader. Encoding is canonical — one fixed field order, every variable-length field length-prefixed, so two callers holding the same record produce identical bytes and an identical digest; follow the framing discipline packages/store/src/recovery-install-codec.ts already uses rather than inventing a second one. Decode is a bounded exact-shape parse, never a cast and never a repair: check the digest BEFORE parsing framing so drifted bytes refuse as a mismatch rather than half-interpreting, refuse trailing bytes, and refuse an extra or missing key. The reader takes the events for a derived aggregate and answers with the record only when ALL of these agree: exactly one event, the exact event type, the payload's own derived aggregate id equals the aggregate it was read from, the event id equals the record's grantId, the predecessor intent/attempt versions match the record's, and the digest verifies. Any disagreement returns the typed refusal with its exact code and layer — unreadable evidence is UNKNOWN and never reconstructed from the parts that did parse. Keep under 250 lines; if it crosses, split the reader out rather than trimming the comments.

ENCODING. Header `moe-activation-ledger/1\n`, then one 4-byte big-endian length-prefixed frame per key in ACTIVATION_LEDGER_RECORD_KEYS order — taken from the frozen key list, never from the caller's key order — each frame holding canonical JSON with object keys sorted recursively. Sealed with a trailing frame carrying sha256 of everything before it, so the bytes are SELF-VERIFYING: decode does not need a digest handed to it alongside. Two callers holding the same record produce identical bytes and digest, asserted directly.

DECODE ORDER, which is the property that matters. splitSealed reads the trailing digest frame WITHOUT parsing anything ahead of it, the digest is compared, and only then is framing parsed — so drifted bytes refuse as DIGEST_MISMATCH rather than being half-interpreted. Trailing bytes refused via `cursor.offset !== body.byteLength`. Fatal TextDecoder, so mis-framed bytes refuse instead of becoming U+FFFD.

RE-ENCODE EQUALITY closes what a digest alone cannot: the decoded record is re-encoded through the production encoder and its digest must equal the sealed one. JSON.parse silently keeps the LAST of two identical keys, so duplicate-key, key-order and whitespace smuggling all survive a digest check over attacker-chosen bytes and die here.

VALIDATION SCOPE is deliberate: this module pins the two version literals, the hex64 activation digest, the three counts, and the sub-fields it cross-checks (effectIntent.aggregateId/idempotencyKey/version, attempt.version, grant.grantId). Producer-owned content is preserved verbatim under the digest rather than re-validated — re-declaring @moe/scheduler's and @moe/runner's validators here would create a second authority that can disagree with the first, which planningNotes explicitly rejected.

READER cross-checks all six conditions and never reconstructs: exactly one event (zero ABSENT, more AMBIGUOUS, neither resolved by picking one), exact event type, payload decodes, the payload's OWN derived aggregate id equals BOTH the aggregate read from and the aggregate the event claims, event id equals grantId, and both successor versions follow their predecessors by exactly one.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the commit adapter, in a new apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.test.ts, driven through a REAL file-backed SqliteEventStore — no fake store, or the test proves only shapes. ACCEPT: one activation commits, and reading the derived aggregate back after REOPENING the file returns the identical record; assert the domain event count for that aggregate is exactly 1 and its event id is the grantId. REPLAY: the SAME command id replays and returns the original durable record with disposition REPLAYED and NO second event — assert the event count is still 1 and, critically, that apply did not rerun (the store runs apply only on EFFECTS_COMMITTED, so a counter proving zero re-execution is the assertion that pins it). CONFLICT: a DISTINCT command for the same (aggregateId, idempotencyKey) pair pins the exact EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT code and layer with zero duplicate events; a distinct command reusing the same grantId on a different aggregate pins the store's uniqueness refusal with its exact code. RACE: two file-backed worker-thread handles released on a shared gate against the same pair produce exactly one acceptance and one coherent refusal, both readers see the same single event after reopen, and the generated race set asserts positive cardinality (results.length === 2). Close every store handle inside the `it` body and in the worker's finally BEFORE posting its result — a handle held across the Windows temp-dir cleanup throws EPERM and kills the vitest worker with zero output. NO PARTIAL TUPLE: with an injected throw between the decision and the event append, assert that after reopen there is no attempt, slot, lease, effect, grant or budget fragment observable for that aggregate — the whole record or nothing. Run and record the RED.

CASES. ACCEPT — commits, reopens, event count exactly 1, event id is the grantId, and the reopened bytes read back through the production reader `toEqual` the original record. REPLAY — same command id and same request bytes returns disposition REPLAYED with the identical record and digest; after reopen the event count is still 1 AND `getAggregateVersion(DERIVED)` is still 1, which is the assertion that actually pins non-rerun: a replay that re-ran the append would leave version 2 even while reporting REPLAYED. NO-APPLY — a delegate records which store methods the adapter called and asserts the call list is exactly ["commitExpectedVersionDecision"], so task rail 1 ("no daemon-owned SQLite objects or DDL") is pinned by a test rather than by intention; reaching for commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply or commitWithApply would fail it. EXPECTED-VERSION CONFLICT — a distinct command on the same (aggregateId, idempotencyKey) pin ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT + layer + outcome REFUSED + storeCode "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", with the aggregate still holding exactly one event whose id is the first grantId. GRANT REUSE — the same grantId on a DIFFERENT derived aggregate pins ACTIVATION_LEDGER_GRANT_ID_CONFLICT + storeCode "DURABLE_ID_CONFLICT", and asserts the other aggregate has zero events. IDEMPOTENCY — the same command id carrying different request bytes pins ACTIVATION_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT + storeCode "IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT". These three refusals are separately assertable, which is what DoD 3 requires and what flattening the upstream code would destroy.

NO PARTIAL TUPLE — a delegate over the REAL store throws instead of forwarding; the adapter must refuse with ACTIVATION_LEDGER_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, and after reopening the file the aggregate has zero events, version 0, and the production reader answers EVIDENCE_ABSENT. All six fragments DoD 5 names (attempt, slot, lease, effect, grant, budget) live in ONE payload, so "no partial fragment" is a structural property; the test asserts the durable consequence rather than asserting the structure back to itself.

RACE — two worker threads on the same file, released on a two-phase SharedArrayBuffer gate (phase 0 releases the open, phase 1 releases the commit, so contention lands on the commit). `expect(results.length).toBe(2)` is asserted FIRST: a race that generated zero results would satisfy every downstream assertion vacuously, which epic rail 6 names explicitly. Exactly one acceptance, exactly one refusal pinned to EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT + layer + storeCode, and after reopen both see the same single event whose id is the WINNER's grantId — a relational check, not merely "some event exists".

WORKER HARNESS, probed before the test was written rather than assumed. A first attempt failed with `Failed to resolve module specifier "@moe/store" ... base scheme is not hierarchical`: a data: URL has no hierarchical base, so bare specifiers cannot resolve from inside one. The fix keeps the boundary on the public root without hardcoding a foreign path — the TEST calls `import.meta.resolve("@moe/store")` (it can resolve the specifier) and hands the resulting URL to the worker; packages/store/package.json confirms `"." : "./src/index.ts"`, so that URL IS the public root. The adapter itself is imported by absolute file URL from import.meta.dirname. Probe verified end to end (`OK {"digest":"4bf5122f","store":"function"}`) with a scratch file created and deleted in the same command.

HANDLE DISCIPLINE against the Windows EPERM failure mode: every handle is closed in a `finally` via withStore, the worker closes its store in `finally` BEFORE posting its result, releaseRace terminates both workers in `finally`, and every wait is bounded — the `it` carries a 30s timeout and worker error/non-zero-exit both reject all three promises, so a dead worker fails by name instead of hanging.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts plus its `.js` bridge. ONE call to the store's existing commitExpectedVersionDecision, and no ad-hoc SQLite: the durable record IS the event payload, so the decision's own `events` array carries {eventId: grant.grantId, eventType: the record's event-type literal, payload: the canonical bytes}. Do NOT reach for commitWithApply/commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply — CommitApply hands out a raw DatabaseSync and exists for callers who write their own tables, which task rail 1 forbids here; the decision path already gives all three properties this DoD needs, and it gives them from authorities that already exist. planningNotes.risks:
1. A NON-INJECTIVE AGGREGATE ID IS THE SILENT CATASTROPHE. Concatenating (aggregateId, idempotencyKey) lets ('a','bc') and ('ab','c') land on one aggregate, where expectedVersion 0 then makes the SECOND activation look like a duplicate of the first — a wrong accept and a wrong refuse from the same bug. Frame the inputs, and drill it (D1).
2. THE APPLY CALLBACK IS A TRAP. It is right there, it takes a DatabaseSync, and using it would violate rail 1 while appearing to satisfy 'one transaction'. The decision path already covers replay, conflict and uniqueness.
3. REPLAY MUST NOT RERUN APPLY — assert it with a counter, not by inspecting the disposition alone; the disposition can read REPLAYED while a side effect still fired if anything is ever moved into the caller.
4. THE PER-FIELD DIGEST SWEEP CAN GO VACUOUS. Assert the swept field count equals the record's own key count, or a field added next quarter is silently unbound. Drill D5 must redden on MANY fields.
5. A REFUSAL TABLE WITHOUT A POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES FOR A READER THAT REFUSES EVERYTHING. Rail 2 requires the accepted control through the same production adapter.
6. HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER. On Windows an open handle makes the temp-dir cleanup throw EPERM and the run dies with zero test output, reading as a native crash. Open and close inside each `it`, and close in the race worker's finally BEFORE posting its result.
7. FLATTENING THE STORE'S UPSTREAM CODE loses the distinction between an expected-version conflict and a uniqueness violation, which DoD 3 requires to be separately assertable. Preserve it verbatim.
8. COUNT THE NOUNS IN DoD 1. It enumerates eight facts plus versions plus digest; an interface that ships seven of them typechecks and passes every test written against itself.
9. SHARED WORKTREE. .moe/**, packages/store/**, packages/contracts/** and adapters/** carry other agents' uncommitted work. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; git add the six new files explicitly before committing by pathspec.
